customManagers.description: Keep the golangci-lint version pinned in the Makefile current - it is run via `go run <module>@<version>`, so no standard manager sees it.
Keep the golangci-lint version passed to golangci/golangci-lint-action in step with the Makefile pin.
Keep the govulncheck version pinned in the Makefile current - it is run via `go run <module>@<version>`, so no standard manager sees it.
Keep the govulncheck version used by the workflow in step with the Makefile pin.
Keep the gotestsum version pinned in the Makefile current - it is run via `go run <module>@<version>`, so no standard manager sees it.
Pin the Firestore emulator image by tag + digest. The same pin appears in the workflow and in docs/firestore-iam.md, so a local run and CI test the same emulator; both are updated together.
Pin the TruffleHog scanner image (version input of trufflesecurity/trufflehog) by version + digest. The action pin alone leaves the image floating.
Keep the Terraform version used by CI in step with the one developers run.
Keep the tflint version used by CI current.
Pin moby/buildkit (setup-buildx-action driver image) by version + digest.
Pin docker/buildkit-syft-scanner (buildx SBOM generator) by version + digest.

packageRules.description: Group GitHub Actions minor/patch into one PR; majors get their own PR.

Group all pre-commit hook updates into one automerged PR - lint/validate-only tooling that never ships and is fully CI-gated. Minor and patch only: a hook is an executable that runs on a developer machine at commit time, so a major bump - which is where a hook changes hands or changes what it runs - is read first.

Go dev tooling run via `go run <module>@<version>` (golangci-lint, govulncheck, gotestsum): never shipped, fully CI-gated. Scoped to the go datasource so it cannot also sweep in the custom managers that pin container images - those execute in CI or inside the release build and are reviewed by hand.
Runtime Go module dependencies: grouped, manual review. This service writes to a live Strava account, so a dependency bump is never unattended.

Renovate disables indirect Go updates by default, which would leave most of the Firestore dependency tree - grpc, the google-api stack, golang.org/x/* - unwatched. They are compiled into the binary and are exactly where govulncheck findings surface, so they are updated too, grouped and reviewed by hand like the direct ones.

Propose go-directive updates at all. Renovate leaves the directive alone by default, because `go 1.x` means "compatible with this version or later" rather than "built with this version", so without rangeStrategy: bump no update is ever generated and the rule below has nothing to act on. This repository does treat it as a pin: CI reads it through `go-version-file: go.mod`, and the Dockerfile's golang tag is bumped by the docker manager, so a directive left behind drifts away from both.
Patch releases of the Go toolchain itself (the `go` directive in go.mod) carry the security fixes; the spec requires staying on latest stable. Minors and majors fall through to manual review.
Automerge digest-only refreshes and initial digest pins (actions + images).

Action and pre-commit digest refreshes are reviewed by hand: minimumReleaseAge cannot hold them back. The datasource ages a digest against the matched version's original release date, so a tag force-pushed to new commits clears the 3-day check immediately and would otherwise automerge within hours. This is the case the pre-commit rule above cannot catch - a hook repo re-pointing an existing tag arrives as a digest update, not a major one.
Terraform providers and modules, and tflint's plugins: grouped, manual review. They describe live infrastructure, and a plan is only as trustworthy as the provider that produced it.
Container base images for the runtime image: grouped and automerged on minor/patch, because CI builds and starts the image on every pull request.

The built-in github-actions manager special-cases golangci/golangci-lint-action and extracts its `version:` input as `golangci/golangci-lint` from github-tags. The custom managers above already pin that same line, together with GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION in the Makefile, as one dependency across both files - which is what keeps the two in step. Leaving both enabled produced two pull requests for one upgrade, editing the same line, so the second to merge would conflict. The custom pair wins because no built-in manager can read the Makefile half.
